items.quote: The Boston Tea Party was an act of protest that took place on December 16, 1773, during the American Revolution
The Freedom Trail is a 2.5 mi path through Boston, Massachusetts, that passes by 16 locations significant to the history of the United States
items.note: Sixteen sites confirmed. Minor: the trail is marked mostly in red brick but partly by a painted red line; harmless for a quiz.

items.quote: The Green Monster is a popular nickname for the 37 ft left field wall at Fenway Park, home to the Boston Red Sox
USS Constitution, also known as Old Ironsides, is a three-masted wooden-hulled heavy frigate of the United States Navy
Old North Church is notable for its role in Paul Revere's midnight ride on April 18, 1775, when two lanterns in the steeple were illuminated
items.note: Easy for anyone who knows "one if by land, two if by sea", but unambiguous.

items.quote: The Boston Marathon was first run in April 1897
items.note: The Boylston Street finish is also stated in the same article ("Its course runs from Hopkinton in southern Middlesex County to Boylston Street, near Copley Square, in Boston").

items.quote: Boston is often referred to as "Beantown" in reference to the popular dish
items.note: The dish in that article is Boston baked beans, "sweetened with molasses". Accept "Boston baked beans".

items.quote: the book centers on a pair of mallards who raise their brood of ducklings on an island in the lagoon in the Boston Public Garden
items.note: In the plot the Mallards first nest on an island in the Charles River and only later move to the Public Garden, so someone may shout "the Charles"; that is a river, not a park, so the question holds. Expect "Boston Common" as the common wrong answer (it adjoins the Public Garden). Accept "Boston Public Garden".

items.quote: It is located in the Greater Boston metropolitan area directly across the Charles River from Boston
Cheers is an American television sitcom, created by Glen Charles & Les Charles and James Burrows, aired on NBC for eleven seasons from September 30, 1982, to May 20, 1993
items.note: Ran 1982 to 1993, so "1980s" is slightly loose; consider "Which long-running NBC sitcom (1982-1993)...". The theme-song lyric plus "Boston bar" makes this a giveaway; fine as a closer.
